title: The incident
description: Sections 2, 3 and 4 of the template: the incident, as each report on it says. Section 2's mandatory fields are mandatory at every stage; the stage decides which of sections 3 and 4 are.

reference_code.title: 2.1 Incident reference code assigned by the financial entity
reference_code.description: The financial entity's own reference for the incident, the same in every report about it. Mandatory in the initial notification, the intermediate report and the final report.

detected_at.title: 2.2 Date and time of detection of the ICT-related incident
detected_at.description: When the incident was detected, in UTC. Mandatory in the initial notification, the intermediate report and the final report.

classified_at.title: 2.3 Date and time of classification of the incident as major
classified_at.description: When the incident was classified as major, in UTC. Mandatory in the initial notification, the intermediate report and the final report.

description.title: 2.4 Description of the ICT-related incident
description.description: What happened and what it affects, in plain words, updated as more is known. Mandatory in the initial notification, the intermediate report and the final report.
examples: Card payments failed for clients of the bank after a configuration change to the payment gateway.

classification_criteria.title: 2.5 Classification criteria that triggered the incident report
classification_criteria.description: Every classification criterion of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1772 the incident met. Mandatory in the initial notification, the intermediate report and the final report.

enum: clients, financial counterparts and transactions affected

geographical_spread_countries.title: 2.6 Materiality thresholds for the classification criterion ‘Geographical spread’
geographical_spread_countries.description: The EEA countries the incident had an impact in, given when 2.5 includes geographical spread. Mandatory when its condition holds.
geographical_spread_countries.x-field-type: Choice (multiple) populated by using ISO 3166 ALPHA-2 of the affected countries

discovery.title: 2.7 Discovery of the major ICT-related incident
discovery.description: How the incident was discovered. Mandatory in the initial notification, the intermediate report and the final report.

originating_provider.title: 2.8 Indication whether the incident originates from a third-party provider or another financial entity
originating_provider.description: The third-party provider or other financial entity the incident originates from, by name and identification code, given when it originates from one. Mandatory when its condition holds.
examples: Example Cloud Ltd;529900EXAMPLE0000078;LEI

business_continuity_plan_activated.title: 2.9 Activation of business continuity plan, if activated
business_continuity_plan_activated.description: Whether the business continuity plan was activated. Mandatory in the initial notification, the intermediate report and the final report.

other_information.title: 2.10 Other relevant information
other_information.description: Anything else the competent authority should know that the template has no field for. Mandatory when its condition holds.
examples: The gateway's previous configuration has been restored.

authority_reference_code.title: 3.1 Incident reference code provided by the competent authority
authority_reference_code.description: The competent authority's reference for the incident, given once it has assigned one. Mandatory when its condition holds.

occurred_at.title: 3.2 Date and time of occurrence of the incident
occurred_at.description: When the incident began, in UTC. Mandatory in the intermediate report and the final report.

restored_at.title: 3.3 Date and time when services, activities or operations have been recovered
restored_at.description: When services, activities and operations were recovered, in UTC, given from the intermediate report on when 3.16 is. Mandatory when its condition holds.

clients_affected.title: 3.4 Number of clients affected
clients_affected.description: How many clients the incident affected. Mandatory in the intermediate report and the final report.

clients_affected_percentage.title: 3.5 Percentage of clients affected
clients_affected_percentage.description: The clients affected, as a percentage of all the financial entity's clients. Mandatory in the intermediate report and the final report.
clients_affected_percentage.x-field-type: Expressed as percentage – any value up to 5 numeric characters including up to 1 decimal place expressed as percentage (e.g. 2,4 instead of 2,4 %). If the value has more than 1 digit after the decimal, reporting counterparties shall round half-up

financial_counterparts_affected.title: 3.6 Number of financial counterparts affected
financial_counterparts_affected.description: How many financial counterparts the incident affected. Mandatory in the intermediate report and the final report.

financial_counterparts_affected_percenta.title: 3.7 Percentage of financial counterparts affected
financial_counterparts_affected_percenta.description: The financial counterparts affected, as a percentage of all of them. Mandatory in the intermediate report and the final report.
financial_counterparts_affected_percenta.x-field-type: Expressed as percentage – any value up to 5 numeric characters including up to 1 decimal place expressed as percentage (e.g. 2,4 instead of 2,4 %). If the value has more than 1 digit after the decimal, reporting counterparties shall round half-up

relevant_clients_or_counterparts_impacte.title: 3.8 Impact on relevant clients or financial counterparts
relevant_clients_or_counterparts_impacte.description: Whether the incident affected clients or financial counterparts that are relevant under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1772, given when that threshold is met. Mandatory when its condition holds.

transactions_affected.title: 3.9 Number of affected transactions
transactions_affected.description: How many transactions the incident affected, given when it affected any. Mandatory when its condition holds.

transactions_affected_percentage.title: 3.10 Percentage of affected transactions
transactions_affected_percentage.description: The transactions affected, as a percentage of the daily average, given when the incident affected any. Mandatory when its condition holds.
transactions_affected_percentage.x-field-type: Expressed as percentage – any value up to 5 numeric characters including up to 1 decimal place expressed as percentage (e.g. 2,4 instead of 2,4 %). If the value has more than 1 digit after the decimal, reporting counterparties shall round half-up

transactions_affected_value.title: 3.11 Value of affected transactions
transactions_affected_value.description: The total value of the transactions affected, in the reporting currency, given when the incident affected any. Mandatory when its condition holds.

impact_figures_basis.title: 3.12 Information on whether the numbers are actual or estimates, or whether there has not been any impact
impact_figures_basis.description: For clients, financial counterparts and transactions in turn, whether 3.4 to 3.11 are actual figures or estimates, or there was no impact. Mandatory in the intermediate report and the final report.

enum: actual figures for financial counterparts affected

reputational_impact.title: 3.13 Reputational impact
reputational_impact.description: How the incident affected the financial entity's reputation, given when 2.5 includes reputational impact. Mandatory when its condition holds.

enum: the major ICT-related incident has been reflected in the media
the major ICT-related incident has resulted in repetitive complaints from different clients or financial counterparts on client-facing services or critical business relationships
the financial entity will not be able to or is likely not to be able to meet regulatory requirements as a result of the major ICT-related incident
the financial entity will or is likely to lose clients or financial counterparts with a material impact on its business as a result of the major ICT-related incident

reputational_impact_context.title: 3.14 Contextual information about the reputational impact
reputational_impact_context.description: What lies behind 3.13, given with it. Mandatory when its condition holds.
examples: Two national newspapers reported the failed payments.

duration.title: 3.15 Duration of the incident
duration.description: How long the incident lasted, from its occurrence to its resolution, or to the report. Mandatory in the intermediate report and the final report.

service_downtime.title: 3.16 Service downtime
service_downtime.description: How long the service was unavailable to clients, given when it was. Mandatory when its condition holds.

duration_figures_basis.title: 3.17 Information on whether the numbers for duration and service downtime are actual or estimates
duration_figures_basis.description: Whether 3.15 and 3.16 are actual figures, estimates or both, given from the intermediate report on when 2.5 includes duration and service downtime. Mandatory when its condition holds.

member_state_impact_types.title: 3.18 Types of impact in the Member States
member_state_impact_types.description: What kind of impact the incident had in the other Member States, given when 2.5 includes geographical spread. Mandatory when its condition holds.

enum: financial entities within the group carrying out activities in the respective Member State
third-party providers that may be common to other financial entities

member_state_impact_description.title: 3.19 Description of how the incident has an impact in other Member States
member_state_impact_description.description: How the incident affected the other Member States, given with 3.18. Mandatory when its condition holds.
examples: Clients of the Austrian branch could not pay by card.

data_losses.title: 3.20 Materiality thresholds for the classification criterion ‘Data losses’
data_losses.description: Which properties of data the incident compromised, given when 2.5 includes data losses. Mandatory when its condition holds.

data_losses_description.title: 3.21 Description of the data losses
data_losses_description.description: What data was compromised and how, given with 3.20. Mandatory when its condition holds.
examples: Payment records for the affected window were written incompletely.

critical_services_affected.title: 3.22 Classification criterion ‘Critical services affected’
critical_services_affected.description: Which critical services the incident affected, and how. Mandatory in the intermediate report and the final report.
examples: Card payment processing for retail clients.

incident_types.title: 3.23 Type of the incident
incident_types.description: What kind of incident it is. Mandatory in the intermediate report and the final report.

other_incident_types.title: 3.24 Other types of incidents
other_incident_types.description: The kind of incident, in words, given from the intermediate report on when 3.23 includes other. Mandatory when its condition holds.
examples: Failed vendor upgrade.

threats_and_techniques.title: 3.25 Threats and techniques used by the threat actor
threats_and_techniques.description: The threats and techniques the attacker used, given from the intermediate report on when 3.23 includes cybersecurity-related. Mandatory when its condition holds.

enum: Data encryption for impact, including ransomware
Data exfiltration and manipulation, including identity theft

other_techniques.title: 3.26 Other types of techniques
other_techniques.description: The techniques, in words, given from the intermediate report on when 3.25 includes other. Mandatory when its condition holds.
examples: Credential stuffing against the administration portal.

affected_functional_areas.title: 3.27 Information about affected functional areas and business processes
affected_functional_areas.description: Which functional areas and business processes the incident affected. Mandatory in the intermediate report and the final report.
examples: Retail payments and the client service desk.

infrastructure_components_affected.title: 3.28 Affected infrastructure components supporting business processes
infrastructure_components_affected.description: Whether infrastructure components that support business processes were affected. Mandatory in the intermediate report and the final report.

infrastructure_components_description.title: 3.29 Information about affected infrastructure components supporting business processes
infrastructure_components_description.description: Which infrastructure components were affected, given from the intermediate report on when 3.28 is Yes. Mandatory when its condition holds.
examples: The payment gateway cluster and its configuration service.

client_financial_interest_impact.title: 3.30 Impact on the financial interest of clients
client_financial_interest_impact.description: Whether the incident affected the financial interests of clients. Mandatory in the intermediate report and the final report.

other_authorities_informed.title: 3.31 Reporting to other authorities
other_authorities_informed.description: Which other authorities the incident has been reported to. Mandatory in the intermediate report and the final report.

other_authorities.title: 3.32 Specification of ‘other’ authorities
other_authorities.description: The other authorities, by name, given from the intermediate report on when 3.31 includes other. Mandatory when its condition holds.
examples: The national consumer protection agency.

temporary_actions.title: 3.33 Temporary actions/measures taken or planned to be taken to recover from the incident
temporary_actions.description: Whether temporary actions or measures have been taken, or are planned, to recover from the incident. Mandatory in the intermediate report and the final report.

temporary_actions_description.title: 3.34 Description of any temporary actions and measures taken or planned to be taken to recover from the incident
temporary_actions_description.description: What the temporary actions and measures are, given from the intermediate report on when 3.33 is true. Mandatory when its condition holds.
examples: The previous gateway configuration was restored and changes were frozen.

indicators_of_compromise.title: 3.35 Indicators of compromise
indicators_of_compromise.description: The indicators of compromise found, given from the intermediate report on when 3.23 includes cybersecurity-related. Mandatory when its condition holds.

root_cause_categories.title: 4.1 High-level classification of root causes of the incident
root_cause_categories.description: The broad kinds of cause behind the incident. Mandatory in the final report.

root_cause_details.title: 4.2 Detailed classification of root causes of the incident
root_cause_details.description: The causes behind the incident, each under its kind of 4.1. Mandatory in the final report.

enum: process failure: insufficient monitoring or failure of monitoring and control
process failure: insufficient/unclear roles and responsibilities
process failure: ICT risk management process failure
process failure: insufficient or failure of ICT operations and ICT security operations
process failure: insufficient or failure of ICT project management
process failure: inadequacy of internal policies, procedures and documentation
Process failure: inadequate ICT systems acquisition, development, and maintenance
system failure: hardware capacity and performance

additional_root_causes.title: 4.3 Additional classification of root causes of the incident
additional_root_causes.description: The finer causes under those categories of 4.2 that the glossary refines, given in the final report when 4.2 reports one of them. Mandatory when its condition holds.

enum: monitoring and verification of remediation of vulnerabilities
failure in specifying accurate risk tolerance levels
poor management of residual ICT risks
ICT asset management and information classification
inadequate ICT systems acquisition, development, and maintenance
insufficient or failure of software testing

other_root_causes.title: 4.4 Other types of root cause types
other_root_causes.description: The causes, in words, given in the final report when 4.2 includes an other. Mandatory when its condition holds.
examples: An undocumented dependency between two configuration keys.

root_cause_information.title: 4.5 Information about the root causes of the incident
root_cause_information.description: What caused the incident, and how the cause was established. Mandatory in the final report.
examples: A configuration change disabled the gateway's fallback route.

resolution_summary.title: 4.6 Incident resolution
resolution_summary.description: How the incident was resolved, and what was done so it does not recur. Mandatory in the final report.
examples: The change was reverted and configuration changes now need two reviewers.

root_cause_addressed_at.title: 4.7 Date and time when the incident root cause was addressed
root_cause_addressed_at.description: When the root cause was addressed, in UTC. Mandatory in the final report.

resolved_at.title: 4.8 Date and time when the incident was resolved
resolved_at.description: When the incident was resolved, in UTC. Mandatory in the final report.

resolution_date_difference.title: 4.9 Information if the permanent resolution date of the incidents differs from the initially planned implementation date
resolution_date_difference.description: Whether the incident was permanently resolved on another date than planned, and why. Mandatory in the final report.
examples: The fix waited for the vendor's patch.

resolution_risk_assessment.title: 4.10 Assessment of risk to critical functions for resolution purposes
resolution_risk_assessment.description: Whether the incident put at risk functions that matter for the entity's resolution, given where resolution authorities need to know. Mandatory when its condition holds.
examples: No critical function for resolution purposes was at risk.

resolution_authority_information.title: 4.11 Information relevant for resolution authorities
resolution_authority_information.description: Anything else resolution authorities should know, given where it applies. Mandatory when its condition holds.
examples: None.

economic_impact_threshold.title: 4.12 Materiality threshold for the classification criterion ‘Economic impact’
economic_impact_threshold.description: What the incident reached of the thresholds of the economic impact criterion. Mandatory in the final report.
examples: The costs and losses stayed below the economic impact threshold.

gross_costs_and_losses.title: 4.13 Amount of gross direct and indirect costs and losses
gross_costs_and_losses.description: The gross direct and indirect costs and losses, in the reporting currency. Mandatory in the final report.

financial_recoveries.title: 4.14 Amount of financial recoveries
financial_recoveries.description: What has been recovered of 4.13, in the reporting currency. Mandatory in the final report.

recurring_incidents.title: 4.15 Information on whether the non-major incidents have been recurring
recurring_incidents.description: Whether the incident is one of recurring incidents that together are major, and what they share, given when it is. Mandatory when its condition holds.
examples: Two earlier failures of the same gateway, each below the thresholds.

recurring_incidents_occurred_at.title: 4.16 Date and time of occurrence of recurring incidents
recurring_incidents_occurred_at.description: When the recurring incidents occurred, in UTC, given in the final report with 4.15. Mandatory when its condition holds.
